title: RE David Snoke v. Pittsburgh Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint found administratively out of order and not capable of being put in order; no merits ruling. Reason: RE Snoke lacked standing to complain against Pittsburgh Presbytery's January 29, 2022 action because he was not a commissioner from his church to that meeting. Presbytery's April 2, 2022 adoption of a motion to find the complaint in order (20-16-3) was contrary to that procedural bar. SJC vote: 20-1, three absent; concurrences noted without separate reasoning.
first_summary: The SJC found RE David Snoke's complaint against Pittsburgh Presbytery administratively out of order. Snoke lacked standing because he was not a commissioner from his church to the January 29, 2022 meeting; Presbytery's later 20-16-3 vote to find the complaint in order did not cure that defect. The SJC cited similar procedural cases and voted 20-1, with three absent.
summary: The SJC held that RE David Snoke's complaint against Pittsburgh Presbytery's January 29, 2022 action was administratively out of order and could not be put in order because Snoke, not a commissioner from his church to that meeting, lacked standing to complain. Although Presbytery later voted 20-16-3 to find the complaint in order, the SJC said it should have been ruled out of order. The SJC did not reach the merits. Its vote was 20-1, with three absent.

evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 17–25, 29: SJC found the complaint administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because Snoke did not have standing—he was not a commissioner from his church to the January 29 meeting. It said Presbytery should have ruled it out of order. SJC vote: 20-1, three absent.

evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Line 27: six prior cases are listed only as examples of similar SJC procedural rulings; no decision is incorporated by reference, so no incorporated result is needed.
